title: Committee of Supply – Head P (Ministry of Home Affairs)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head P (Ministry of Home Affairs)

sections.label: Budget cut for Head P
sections.summary: A motion is moved to reduce the total sum allocated for Head P of the Estimates by $100.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head P of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

sections.label: Community approach to counter terrorism
sections.summary: The Government facilitates but all Singaporeans must play a part in a community, holistic approach to counter terrorism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: While the Government can play a facilitating role, ultimately, every Singaporean needs to play a part.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This community, holistic approach to counter terrorism is supported by a recent study that showed that Malaysia's previous terrorist rehabilitation programme was perhaps not all that effective as it was a top-down and only focused on the religious aspect of violent extremism, with the majority of rehabilitated, or so-called rehabilitated terrorists, still holding on to their original beliefs and continuing financial support to violent groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In contrast, Indonesia's variety of rehabilitation programmes run by the government, civil society groups and the local community was more comprehensive in addressing the variety of factors, taking into account the person's feelings of dissatisfaction with life, weak ties with family members, poverty and ideology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Last year, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) announced that by 2019, every one of the 89 constituencies will have undergone at least one crisis response exercise.

sections.label: Internet link in radicalisation cases
sections.summary: A Straits Times article reported the Internet was a common link in 15 radicalised Singaporean ISA cases since 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: A Straits Times' article in July last year reported that the Internet was a common link in all 15 cases of Singaporeans who were radicalised and dealt with under the Internal Security Act (ISA) since 2014.

sections.label: Increased religiosity in nearby countries
sections.summary: A trend of increased religiosity has been observed in countries around Singapore, including a Johor launderette offering Muslim-only services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, in the last few years, we have observed a trend of increased religiosity in countries around us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Members would recall the incident where a launderette owner in Johor offered "Muslim-only" services to their customers.

sections.label: Loan shark cases and citizenship statistics
sections.summary: CCTV and enforcement cut loan shark harassment since 2010 but cases spiked last year, and no official statistics detail new citizens' countries of origin.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The widespread use of Police closed-circuit television (CCTV) surveillance in public housing estates and tough enforcement have led to the steady decline of loan shark harassment cases since 2010.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But there is a spike in cases last year for the first time, with electronic harassment contributing to the spike.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify whether this spike also represents a spike in Singaporeans borrowing from loan sharks?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, as a country that extends Singapore citizenship to an average 20,000 foreigners each year and partly relies extensively on immigration to replace and increase the overall population, it remains an anomaly that there are no official statistics detailing the country of origin of new citizens who live among us and who have to integrate together with us as one people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Previously, it was revealed that about 50% of new citizens originate from Southeast Asian countries, with another 40% from other Asian countries.

sections.label: Income and PR status concerns
sections.summary: Some residents worry their monthly household income explains difficulty securing PR status, with about 45% of foreign-spouse PRs from 2009-2015 earning under $4,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, in my discussion with some residents in my Meet-the-People sessions (MPS), there is some residual concern amongst such residents that their monthly household income explains why they are having trouble securing Permanent Resident status.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I understand from previous PQs that for foreign spouses who were granted PR from 2009 to 2015, around 45% had a monthly income of less than $4,000.

sections.label: MSF unit handling cases
sections.summary: A unit set up by the Ministry of Social and Family Development in May 2015 dealt with over 100 such cases in its first year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: A unit set up by the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) in May 2015 dealt with over 100 such cases in its first year.

sections.label: Sexual assault on minors
sections.summary: In 2014, the attacker in 90% of criminal cases involving sexual assault on a minor was someone supposed to protect the child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: The attacker in 90% of the criminal cases involving sexual assault on a minor in 2014 was someone who was supposed to protect the child.

sections.label: Amendments on mentally-challenged offenders
sections.summary: Amendments allow mandatory treatment orders for mentally-challenged offenders, and the Criminal Justice Reform Bill proposes expanding community sentencing and recognising inpatient treatment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Through these amendments, mentally-challenged offenders may be imposed a mandatory treatment order in lieu of the usual sentences, such as an imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We just saw the introduction of the Criminal Justice Reform Bill where it is proposed to expand the spectrum of offences for which a community sentence may be imposed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I am particularly happy to note that the Government has kept an open mind on a point I raised in my PQ in May 2017 and now intends to allow community sentencing to be imposed on offences punishable by specified minimum sentences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Inpatient treatment will be recognised as being part of the mandatory treatment order regime, if the Bill is passed.

sections.label: Repeat offenders and conditional warnings
sections.summary: Repeat offenders with mental conditions often receive conditional warnings, and a treatment and rehabilitation regime akin to a mandatory treatment order is suggested.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For repeat offenders, in light of their mental conditions, it is not unusual for them to be imposed conditional warnings, meaning so long as they do not reoffend for a specified period of time, they would not be prosecuted for the offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I would respectfully suggest that there is an opportunity here to introduce a system that would allow them to subscribe to a treatment and rehabilitation regime, akin to a mandatory treatment order (MTO), so that the chances of them reoffending is kept low.

sections.label: Conditions for boy's rehabilitation
sections.summary: Instead of a traditional conditional warning for trespass, further conditions and a regime supported by his parents may give the boy the best chance for rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Instead of issuing the traditional conditional warning telling the boy not to reoffend, failing which he would be charged in Court for the offence of trespass, it may be useful to work in further conditions and require him to subscribe to a regime, with the support of his parents, so that we can provide him with the best chance for rehabilitation.

sections.label: New drug abuser statistics
sections.summary: The contamination rate remains high, with new drug abusers at about 40% and those under 30 at about two-thirds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Statistics show that the contamination rate is still high, with the proportion of new drug abusers remaining high at about 40%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: The proportion of new drug abusers under 30 years of age also remains high, at about two-thirds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: In the past four years, the age group of those between 20 and 29 has made up about 45% to 50% of new abusers each year.

sections.label: Methamphetamine share of new abusers
sections.summary: Methamphetamine abusers make up 80% of all new abusers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: For new abusers, methamphetamine abusers also account for the highest proportion, being 80% of all new abusers.

sections.label: Indonesian seizure on Singapore-flagged ship
sections.summary: Indonesian authorities seized 1.6 tonnes of crystal meth hidden on a Singapore-flagged ship between Sumatra and Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In fact, just last week, Indonesian authorities seized 1.6 tonnes of crystal meth, hidden on a Singapore-flagged ship, plying the waters between Sumatra and Singapore.

sections.label: 2017 drug abuser arrests decrease
sections.summary: CNB February statistics show total drug abusers arrested in 2017 fell about 5% from the previous year.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Based on the statistics released by CNB in February, the total number of drug abusers arrested in 2017 decreased by about 5% from the previous year.

sections.label: New drug offender arrest statistics
sections.summary: About two-thirds of new drug offenders arrested last year were under 30, and new abusers formed 40% of all drug abusers arrested in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: About two-thirds of the new drug offenders arrested last year were below the age of 30, similar to that of 2016.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: New drug abusers formed 40% of all drug abusers arrested in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The figure was 13 in 2015 and 201 in 2016.

sections.label: Families pay price, Malay over-representation
sections.summary: Family members pay a price for the crime, and the Malay community is over-represented among drug offenders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The family members may have not been the ones who have been the addict, but they also have to pay a price for the crime.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: I note that the Malay community is over-represented amongst the drug-offenders.

sections.label: Programmes for inmates in initial months
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to consider more programmes featuring ex-offenders during inmates' initial two to three months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Can the Ministry consider including more programmes featuring ex-offenders and imparting life-changing strategies at this initial stage, especially during the initial two to three months, when inmates are most motivated to change and commitments are more sustainable?

sections.label: Children's Day prison open visit
sections.summary: An MP asks whether the Ministry can extend the open visit programme, where 24 inmates could hug loved ones, to more inmates and hold such visits more often.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The Children’s Day event at Tanah Merah Prison last year, where 24 inmates were allowed an open visit where they could hug and hold their loved ones instead of being separated by a glass panel, was an excellent event.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Can the Ministry extend this programme to more inmates and conduct more of such visits more often?

sections.label: Ex-offender employment and skills training
sections.summary: An MP seeks an update on plans to enhance employment assistance and skills-training for ex-offenders, and says prisoners must have access to education and skills training during incarceration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Ex-offenders, facing difficulties finding work or at work, will be tempted or even compelled to return to familiar old, bad habits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to seek an update on the Ministry's plans to enhance employment assistance and skills-training for ex-offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: During incarceration, prisoners must have access to relevant education and skills training as part of their rehabilitation.

sections.label: Ex-offender reintegration and stigma
sections.summary: An MP notes the 2005 amendment of the Registration of Criminals Act, describes reintegration networks, and asks what further steps can enhance an ex-offender's reintegration into society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: For instance, the Registration of Criminals Act was amended in 2005 to allow those convicted of less serious crimes to have their record considered spent if they did not re-offend for a period of five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Rehabilitation and, particularly, reintegration of ex-offenders as responsible citizens have become one of the core tenets of our criminal justice system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Reintegration, however, is a prolonged process, not one-off.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Hence, the various networks set up to link up the various organisations, including voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs), the groups affiliated with the National Council of Social Services (NCSS), MSF, Statutory Boards like the Singapore Corporation of Rehabilitative Enterprises (SCORE), or the Yellow Ribbon Project, which is most well-known, are all useful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But I would suggest that much more is needed to change the attitude and perception the society has towards ex-offenders, in order that the prejudice and stigma of reintegration into society does not become as much of a bar in society as it was in prison for the ex-offender.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In that context, can I ask the Minister what further steps can be taken to enhance an ex-offender's reintegration back into society?

sections.label: New drug abusers arrested 2017
sections.summary: According to the CNB, the proportion of new drug abusers arrested in 2017 remained high and close to two-thirds were under 30.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: According to the CNB, the proportion of new drug abusers arrested in 2017 remained high and close to two-thirds of new abusers were under 30.

sections.label: Online scams among older users
sections.summary: The number of online scams has been increasing and becoming more pervasive, especially amongst older users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The number of online scams has been increasing and becoming more pervasive, especially amongst the older users.

sections.label: Converting officers to civilian roles
sections.summary: An MP asks whether these officers could be converted into civilian officers for other security-related responsibilities, and notes the terrorism threat remains at its highest level in recent years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Could these officers be converted into civilian officers and deployed to take on other security-related responsibilities in the public or private space?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: These officers may also be able to raise the capabilities and support the needs of the private security sector under the Industry Transformation Map (ITM) that was launched just this month.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the terrorism threat remains at its highest level in recent years.

sections.label: Security courses and industry transformation
sections.summary: An MP asks whether MHA can guide course organisers to teach security skills accessibly, and what plans exist to transform the private security industry.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I ask whether MHA can help guide the organisers of such courses, so that security skills can be taught in a way that is more accessible to Singaporeans of different educational and language backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: More broadly, I also ask what plans there are to transform the private security industry so that we can continue having better working conditions, career prospects and wages for our workers.

sections.label: Infrastructure Protection Act enactment
sections.summary: The Infrastructure Protection Act was enacted last year to enhance protection of certain Singapore infrastructure against security risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Infrastructure Protection Act (IPA) was enacted last year to enhance the protection of certain infrastructure in Singapore against security risk.

sections.label: Security ITM and WSQ launch
sections.summary: Second Minister Josephine Teo launched the security ITM and a new Workforce Skills Qualifications pathway for security consultancy leading to a specialist diploma.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: At the launch of the security ITM, Second Minister Josephine Teo, who also launched a new Workforce Skills Qualifications (WSQ) pathway for security consultancy leading to a new specialist diploma in security consultancy.

sections.label: Singapore safety rankings and crime
sections.summary: Singapore ranked first in the Gallup Global Law and Order Report 2017 and second in the Safe Cities Index 2017, with crime at an all-time low.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I thank the hon Members for their comments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We were ranked No 1 in the Gallup Global Law and Order Report 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Economist Intelligence Unit's Safe Cities Index 2017 ranked us second, behind Tokyo.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Ninety-seven percent of our residents feel safe walking home alone at night.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Crimes, such as robbery, housebreakings and snatch thefts, registered an all-time low in 2017.

sections.label: MHA budget increase
sections.summary: MHA's budget has increased by more than 10% this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: MHA's budget has increased by more than 10% this year.

sections.label: Marital rape immunity review
sections.summary: Removal of immunity against marital rape is being studied, and violence against women is wrong.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng asked about marital rape, and that is also under review.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Violence against women is wrong – no ifs and no buts on that.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, removal of immunity against marital rape is being studied.

sections.label: Officer training and OneSAFE Centre
sections.summary: A group of officers was selected and started training, and the One-Stop Abuse Forensic Examination (OneSAFE) Centre was introduced.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Some examples of the changes that have been made, we have selected and started training a group of officers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We have introduced the One-Stop Abuse Forensic Examination (OneSAFE) Centre.

sections.label: Multi-Disciplinary Interview pilot
sections.summary: In June this year, the Police, with KK Women's and Children's Hospital and other partners, will pilot a Multi-Disciplinary Interview model.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In June this year, the Police, together with KK Women’s and Children’s Hospital (KKH) and other partners, will pilot a Multi-Disciplinary Interview (MDI) model.

sections.label: Home Team Community Assistance Scheme
sections.summary: A new scheme will be called the Home Team Community Assistance and Referral Scheme (HT CARES).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: This is something new, in the sense of what I am going to say.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: It will be called the Home Team Community Assistance and Referral Scheme (HT CARES).

sections.label: Reduced minimum detention period
sections.summary: One change is to reduce the minimum detention period from the current 18 months to either six months or 12 months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: One of these changes is to reduce the minimum detention period from the current 18 months to either six months or 12 months.

sections.label: Ban on foreign preachers
sections.summary: In September last year, two foreign preachers were banned.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In September last year, we banned two foreign preachers: Christian.

sections.label: Ban on Muslim preachers
sections.summary: In October 2017, two foreign Muslim preachers, Mufti Ismail Menk and Haslin bin Baharim, were refused.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: A month later, in October 2017, we said no to two foreign Muslim preachers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: One was Mufti Ismail Menk, and the other is Haslin bin Baharim.

sections.label: Bus incident after detention news
sections.summary: After news of Syaikhah Izzah Zahrah Al Ansari's detention, an Indian man scolded a Muslim woman on a bus, saying Muslims should stay in Iraq.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In June last year, after the news of the detention of Syaikhah Izzah Zahrah Al Ansari was reported, we had an Indian man scolding a Muslim lady who wore a tudung on a bus, saying that Muslims "should stay in Iraq as they did not know the value   staying in Singapore".

sections.label: Youth attitudes towards drugs survey
sections.summary: A 2016 survey shows young people more open to drugs, especially cannabis, which research says harms teenagers' brains.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The results from a 2016 National Council Against Drug Abuse survey shows a slightly worrying trend.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Our young people are adopting a slightly more open attitude towards drugs, compared with a similar survey done three years earlier in 2013, especially towards cannabis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I think the Internet, social media, the pro-legalisation lobby in the US are telling them it is cool and safe to take cannabis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But if you look at the well-supported research, it tells us that cannabis is harmful, especially to teenagers, because it can cause irreversible brain damage.

sections.label: US drug overdose deaths 2016
sections.summary: The US National Centre for Health Statistics estimated almost 64,000 people died from drug overdose in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The US National Centre for Health Statistics estimated almost 64,000 people died from drug overdose in 2016.

sections.label: Portugal drug use after decriminalisation
sections.summary: The lifetime prevalence of drug use in Portugal has increased since decriminalisation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The lifetime prevalence of drug use in Portugal has increased since decriminalisation.

sections.label: Opiate abusers Singapore versus US
sections.summary: Singapore has fewer than 30 opiate abusers per 100,000 people, compared with 600 in the US.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For example, the number of opiate abusers in Singapore is less than 30 per 100,000 people.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In the US, the number is 600, that is, 20 times our number.

sections.label: HIV transmission and drug arrests
sections.summary: Intravenous drug use is not a significant mode of HIV transmission in Singapore, and annual drug arrests have fallen from near 7,000 to over 3,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Intravenous drug use is not a significant mode of HIV transmission in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, if you think of the lives that have been saved, the misery, deprivation, the loss – we have saved a lot of people from that, if you just look at that slide ‒ from something near 7,000 people being arrested per year, to something in the region of 3,000-plus being arrested now.

sections.label: Regional drug trafficking profits
sections.summary: Trafficking of heroin and methamphetamine in this region is estimated to generate over US$32 billion annually, attracting international criminal syndicates.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Trafficking of heroin and methamphetamine in this region alone is estimated to generate over US$32 billion annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: International criminal syndicates operate in this region, attracted by the profits.

sections.label: Threat level to Singapore
sections.summary: The threat to Singapore is at its highest level in recent years.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The threat to Singapore is at its highest level in recent years.

sections.label: Public Order and Safety Bill debate
sections.summary: Later this month, Parliament will debate the Public Order and Safety (Special Powers) Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Later this month, Parliament will debate the Public Order and Safety (Special Powers) Bill.

sections.label: In-Situ Reaction Teams

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In December last year, we put in place In-Situ Reaction Teams.

sections.label: SGSecure Guide for Workplaces

sentences.text: We spend quite a lot of time at the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Our annual investment in technology infrastructure alone – and, by that, I am referring to sensors and sense-making, for example, the Command, Control and Communication systems – is projected to triple over the next two years.

sections.summary: SCDF handles about 183,000 emergency calls a year, and projections show the number will double by around 2030.

sentences.text: Chairman, in terms of emergency calls, SCDF now handles about 183,000 calls a year.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: That translates to 500 calls a day and about one every three minutes.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And based on SCDF's projections, the number of emergency services calls will double by around 2030.

sections.label: Survey on terrorist attack preparedness
sections.summary: 77% named terrorist attacks as a top focus for emergency preparedness training, but only 30% felt well-prepared for one in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: When asked "Which are the top three potential situations they thought the Government should focus emergency preparedness training on?" 77% said terrorist attacks.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But when they were asked if they believed they were well-prepared to handle a terrorist attack if it were to occur in Singapore, only 30% said yes.
